title_ar: الشيخ الددو يترأس الحفل الختامي لمركز تكوين العلماء للعام الدراسي 1436هـ
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Chairs the Closing Ceremony of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars for the Academic Year 1436 AH
body_ar: ترأس فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو –حفظه الله تعالى- الحفل الختامي لمركز تكوين العلماء للعامي الدراسي 1436هـ الموافق 2014/ 2015م، والذي نظم يوم الخميس 23/07/2015م، تحت شعار "من جد وجد ". وقد بدأ الشيخ كلمته مرحبا بورثة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حاملي مشعل الهداية والنور إلى الناس { الذي يبلغون رسالات الله ويخشونه ولا يخشون أحدا إلى الله }، مثمنا ما يشتغلون به مؤكدا أن الجميع شركاء في أجر المركز من رجال الأعمال الذين يرعون المركز و العلماء الربانيبن ورجال المجتمع وقادة الرأي فيه الذين هم من أشرعة المركز و الذابين عنه وكذلك الأخوات اللواتي سعين لإرفاد هذا المركز بكل ما يحتاج إليه وكذلك رجال الإعلام الذين يبلغون رسالة المركز وينشرونها بين الناس بكل أمانة. مضيفا أن المركز لم ينشأ ليكون رقما يضاف إلى المؤسسات التعليمية في البلد وإنما أنشئ ليكون مركزا عالميا لتكوين العلماء، ومن أجل ذلك وضع برنامجين أحدهما البرنامج العلمي حيث يتناول 63 تخصصا، سيكون بعدها الطالب خلال 17 سنة بمثابة 63 وستين دكتورا في كل التخصصات الشرعية واللغوية، والثاني البرنامج التربوي الذي يهتم بتربية العلماء وصلتهم بالله. بعد ذلك رحب فضيلة الشيخ بالضيوف الكرام كل بإسمه ووصفه، ثم خاطب طلاب المركز قائلا أنتم ورثة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، موضحا أن طلب العلم مزية كريمة، حيث قال إنهم يريدون أن يكون أدنى الطلاب خيرا من أرفع القائمين على المركز رتبة. ثم شكر الشيخ مشاييخ المركز قائلا: جزاكم الله خيرا، فأنت أنصار هذا الزمان فقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الأنصار "إنهم أدو الذي عليكم وبقي الذي لكم". كما شكر فضيلته الإخوة في الإدارة على ما بذلوا من جهود مضنية من أجل إسعاد الآخرين، متمثلا فيهم قول الإمام أحمد بن حنبل "الحمد لله الذي جعل في كل بقية من الناس ورثة للرسل يحملون أمانات الله فيؤدونها بأمانة فما أحسن أثرهم على الناس وما أسوء أثر الناس عليهم" وقال فضيلة الشيخ مخاطبا الذين جاؤوا وحضروا لتتويج المركز وعمله نسأل الله أن يتقبل منكم أجمعين فأنتم مشكورون ومأجورون وخطاهم مكتوبة غير ضائعة إن شاء الله ذاكرا أن من نسيه ولم ينوه بإسمه فهو حاضر في البال ولكن قربه حاضر دون ذكره، فالترحيب موصل بالجميع.
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him) chaired the closing ceremony of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars for the academic year 1436 AH, corresponding to 2014/2015, held on Thursday 23/07/2015 under the motto 'Whoever strives, finds'.

The Sheikh began his address by welcoming the heirs of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), the bearers of the torch of guidance and light to the people — {those who convey the messages of God and fear Him and fear none but God} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:39) — valuing what they are engaged in, and affirming that all are partners in the Centre's reward: the businessmen who support the Centre; the godly scholars; the men of the society and its opinion leaders, who are among the Centre's sails and its defenders; likewise the sisters who have worked to furnish this Centre with everything it needs; and likewise the media people, who convey the Centre's message and spread it among the people in all trustworthiness.

He added that the Centre was not founded to be one more number added to the country's educational institutions, but was founded to be a world centre for the formation of scholars. To that end it has laid out two programmes. The first is the academic programme, which takes in 63 specialisms, after which the student, over 17 years, will be the equivalent of sixty-three doctors in every one of the Sharia and linguistic specialisms. The second is the formative programme, which attends to the moral formation of scholars and to their connection with God.

His Eminence then welcomed the honoured guests, each by name and description, and then addressed the Centre's students, saying: you are the heirs of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) — explaining that seeking knowledge is a noble distinction, and saying that they want the lowest of the students to be better than the highest in rank of those who run the Centre.

The Sheikh then thanked the Centre's teaching shaykhs, saying: "May God reward you well; you are the Ansar of this age" — for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said of the Ansar: "They have discharged what was upon them, and what is theirs remains."

His Eminence also thanked the brothers in the administration for the exhausting efforts they have expended in order to bring happiness to others, applying to them the words of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal: "Praise be to God, who has placed in every remnant of the people heirs of the messengers, who carry God's trusts and discharge them faithfully. How good is their effect upon the people, and how evil is the people's effect upon them."

Addressing those who had come and been present to crown the Centre and its work, the Sheikh said: we ask God to accept from you all, for you are thanked and rewarded, and their steps are written down and not lost, God willing — noting that anyone he had overlooked and not named was present in his mind, and that such a person's closeness was present without being mentioned; the welcome reaches everyone.

flags.arabic: { الذي يبلغون رسالات الله ويخشونه ولا يخشون أحدا إلى الله }
flags.context: the Qur'anic text quoted at the opening of the address
options: read as الذين … ولا يخشون أحدا إلا الله (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:39)
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, SCRIPTURE (house rule 11). Two errors in five words of Qur'anic text: الذي for الذين, and إلى for إلا — the second of which reverses the sense, turning 'they fear none but God' into something ungrammatical that reads towards 'they fear no one towards God'. Preserved unchanged in body_ar; the English translates the Qur'anic text and supplies the reference the source omits. The lacuna is left visible here rather than silently repaired in the Arabic.

flags.arabic: "إنهم أدو الذي عليكم وبقي الذي لكم"
flags.context: the report about the Ansar quoted in thanks to the teachers
options: read as أدَّوا الذي عليهم وبقي الذي لهم
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11). The report speaks about the Ansar in the third person — 'they have discharged what was upon them, and what is theirs remains' — but the source puts the pronouns in the second person, عليكم and لكم, which does not construe with إنهم. Preserved in body_ar; the English uses the third person the sentence requires. The Sheikh gives no narrator or collection.

flags.arabic: سيكون بعدها الطالب خلال 17 سنة بمثابة 63 وستين دكتورا
flags.context: the description of the academic programme
options: read as بمثابة ثلاثة وستين دكتورا, matching the 63 specialisms named in the same sentence
the figure is garbled beyond recovery
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): the numeral 63 is followed by وستين, 'and sixty', producing '63 and sixty doctors'. The sentence has just named 63 specialisms, so the intended figure is plainly sixty-three. Preserved unchanged in body_ar and translated on the required reading. The claim itself — that a student completes the equivalent of sixty-three doctorates in seventeen years — is the Centre's own and is reproduced without comment.

flags.arabic: "الحمد لله الذي جعل في كل بقية من الناس ورثة للرسل…"
flags.context: the saying attributed to Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
options: reproduce the source's wording: 'in every remnant of the people'
the familiar form of the saying runs 'in every interval between the messengers, remnants of the people of knowledge'
flags.note: The saying is Ahmad's well-known preface to al-Radd ʿalā al-Zanādiqah, usually transmitted as في كل زمان فترة من الرسل بقايا من أهل العلم. The wording here is a compression, whether the Sheikh's, the reporter's or the CMS's. Translated as the source has it and not replaced with the familiar version.

flags.arabic: البرنامج التربوي الذي يهتم بتربية العلماء
flags.context: the second of the Centre's two programmes
options: the formative programme, attending to the moral formation of scholars
the educational programme, attending to the upbringing of scholars
flags.note: تربية here is formation of character and religious life, set against the علمي programme of learning; 'educational' would collapse the contrast the sentence is built on. تكوين in the Centre's own name is rendered 'formation' throughout, and تربية is distinguished from it as 'moral formation'.

flags.arabic: العلماء الربانيبن / مشاييخ / بإسمه / ما أسوء / للعامي الدراسي / فأنت أنصار
options: read as الربانيين / مشايخ / باسمه / ما أسوأ / للعام الدراسي / فأنتم أنصار
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECTS (house rule 11), recorded together: a transposed letter, a doubled yāʾ, two hamza errors, a case ending and a singular for a plural. All preserved unchanged in body_ar. This record carries an unusually high density of CMS typing errors, which is itself worth noting when the corpus is cleaned globally.

translator_notes: A news report of an address, mixing indirect report with two short direct quotations. Most of the English is the site's account of what the Sheikh said and must not be cited as his wording.
من جد وجد, the ceremony's motto, is a rhyming proverb ('whoever strives, finds'); the rhyme is not reproducible in English and no attempt has been made.
من أشرعة المركز rendered 'among the Centre's sails' — the image is of what drives the ship forward, and it is kept rather than replaced with an explanation.
The final sentence is grammatically tangled in the Arabic, shifting between second and third person; the English follows the shifts rather than smoothing them.
Qur'anic renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
